item.title: PFT's Week 5 2026 NFL picks
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Our take on all 15 games to be played this weekend.
item.content:encoded:
I've got a problem when it comes to guessing who'll win the standalone games. Basically, I currently suck.

For the games that had the stage to themselves in Week 4, I was 0-4. Fortunately, I was otherwise 10-2. And a final result of 10-6 is better than the Week 3 mark of 8-8.

But every week is a clean slate. A new opportunity to turn 0-0 into something that isn't embarrassing.

For the year, I'm 37-27. Which is good, but far from great. At least it's not horrible, which is mainly what I'm trying to avoid.

The best pick for Week 4 was the 49ers over the Broncos. Worst pick: Lions over Panthers. Flew too close to the sun on wings of pastrami pick: Saints over Falcons.

My seat-of-the-pants prognostications for all 15 of the Week 5 appear below, one wild-ass guess at a time. (The Panthers and Chiefs are off, as the bye weeks begin.)

Buccaneers at Cowboys (Thursday night)

Could undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels make a big splash in prime time? Yes, especially if the Cowboys take the Buccaneers too lightly. Every Tampa loss has come in a one-score game. If the Bucs can withstand the early onslaught, they have a chance.

I'll lean toward the Cowboys not being caught napping, and the Bucs not being able to avoid slipping into an early hole against an offense that is still trying to live up to its self-applied nickname.

Cowboys 34, Buccaneers 13.

Eagles vs. Jaguars (London)

The Eagles went from 2-0 with plenty of questions to 2-2 with few answers. Given the injuries and the roster turmoil, it will take all of coach Nick Sirianni's abilities and then some to engineer a win after a flight to London. And it will require the Jaguars to regard the Eagles as an early bye week.

Jaguars 27, Eagles 12.

Bears at Packers

In any divisional game, anything can happen. But the Bears, even without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, have the better team. They also have a head coach who needs to back up his big talk about Chicago's top rival.

Bears 27, Packers 20.

Bengals at Dolphins

Miami simply isn't good enough, on either side of the ball. The Bengals, who have big aspirations, can't afford to lose their third in a row — especially in a game they absolutely should win.

Bengals 26, Dolphins 14.

Raiders at Patriots

Last year, the Raiders went to Gillette Stadium and gave the Patriots a dry shave with a rusty razor. The Patriots, who rediscovered their swagger at Buffalo, surely remember that. If they don't, coach Mike Vrabel will spend the entire week reminding them of it.

Patriots 27, Raiders 24.

Vikings at Saints

The Vikings' strong finish to 2025 has carried over. The Saints' strong finish to 2025 has not.

Vikings 23, Saints 17.

Browns at Jets

How good are the 2026 Browns? I didn't even think twice about this one.

Browns 17, Jets 10.

Colts at Steelers

Pittsburgh's schedule suddenly has plenty of winnable games on it. This week, the Steelers go three extra days to get ready, and the Colts had to fly back from London.

Steelers 24, Colts 20.

Texans at Titans

Not even The Weather Channel wants to televise this one. If the Texans can't finagle a win, their remaining games should land on public-access TV.

Texans 21, Titans 16.

Giants at Commanders

Jayden Daniels's return should give the Commanders a spark. As long as the brace he'll be wearing on his elbow works.

Commanders 27, Giants 23.

Broncos at Chargers

Sean Payton picked the right spot to get back into calling plays. Still, it's a sudden must-win game for a team that has much higher aspirations than just making it to the playoffs.

Broncos 27, Chargers 17.

Lions at Cardinals

Whether Dan Campbell likes it or not, the Lions are mediocre. Fortunately for Detroit, the Cardinals are less than mediocre.

Lions 24, Cardinals 23.

49ers at Seahawks

The Seahawks can't afford to fall two games behind the 49ers. And Seattle vividly remembers losing at home to San Francisco last year.

Seahawks 21, 49ers 17.

Ravens at Falcons (Sunday night)

A Ravens team without Lamar Jackson is no match for the prime-time Falcons.

Falcons 30, Ravens 21.

Bills at Rams (Monday night)

This potential Super Bowl preview won't be if the Rams can't start winning more consistently.

Rams 38, Bills 35.

item.title: Steelers WR Michael Pittman Jr. will miss multiple games after re-injuring his foot
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. won't play against his former team when the Colts come to town on Sunday, and he won't play for a while after that, either.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. won't play against his former team when the Colts come to town on Sunday, and he won't play for a while after that, either.

Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy said today that Pittman will miss time after re-injuring his foot, and it's too soon to say whether he will have to go on injured reserve.

"It's the same foot, so it's going to be a multiple-week injury," McCarthy said. "We're still going through the evaluation of his roster position."

The Steelers traded for Pittman in March and signed him to a three-year, $59 million contract extension, but so far that hasn't looked like a great investment. Pittman has just seven catches for 89 yards this season.

A 2020 second-round pick of the Colts out of USC, Pittman had two 1,000-yard receiving seasons in Indianapolis and appeared to have a long and promising career ahead of him, but his production declined over the last couple seasons with the Colts, and now the Steelers' primary focus will be on getting him healthy.

item.title: Tucker Kraft on dropped passes: I'm trying to do too much
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Packers tight end Tucker Kraft's return from last season's torn ACL hasn't been without its bumps.
item.content:encoded:
Packers tight end Tucker Kraft's return from last season's torn ACL hasn't been without its bumps.

Kraft caught his first touchdown of the season in last Sunday's win over the Buccaneers, but he also failed to reel in another Jordan Love pass that would have points on the board for the Packers. The drop was not the anomaly that it would have been in past seasons.

Kraft has been credited with five dropped passes through four weeks, which matches his highest total for an entire season.

“I think I’m just trying to do too much,” Kraft said, via Steve Megaree of the Associated Press. “Offensively, we might get into a lull, and I think I can make the game-saving play right there. I’m taking my eyes off the ball. Can’t do anything without the ball, so I’m just going to slow down and play my role. Catch the football.”

Kraft's play prior to the injury earned him a long-term deal before the season and he said his "goal is always to ascend" beyond where he was in the past. Kraft noted that starts with catching the ball and the hope in Green Bay is that he'll be doing that with fewer issues over the rest of the season.

item.title: David Blough: Jayden Daniels is full go, looking forward to having him back Sunday
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is good to go for Sunday's game against the Giants.
item.content:encoded:
Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is good to go for Sunday's game against the Giants.

That's the word from Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough, who said there are no challenges or limitations with what Daniels will be able to do on Sunday.

"He's full go, man. We're looking forward to having him back."

Daniels was a full participant in practice yesterday, his first full practice since suffering a dislocated left elbow in Week 2. Marcus Mariota played fairly well in place of Daniels, but Mariota is now injured as well and the next quarterback up is seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis.

The Commanders are 3.5-point favorites against the Giants on Sunday, which demonstrates that the bettors believe Daniels will be Washington's quarterback.

item.title: Jacoby Brissett: Last three losses have upped urgency, but there's no panic
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: After defeating the Chargers to open the 2026 season, the Cardinals have dropped three straight to the Seahawks, 49ers, and Giants.
item.content:encoded:
After defeating the Chargers to open the 2026 season, the Cardinals have dropped three straight to the Seahawks, 49ers, and Giants.

But the results haven’t made things dire inside Arizona’s building, according to quarterback Jacoby Brissett — just upped the urgency a bit.

“I think the sense of urgency needs to be there no matter what the record is,” Brissett said in his Wednesday press conference. “Each week is a 1-0 league. I think the way the last three weeks have ended has definitely created another sense of urgency, but obviously not a sense of panic.

“You can’t panic. The urgency can be there and it’s like how can we steady the ship without everybody trying to jump off the ship or pick up the ship and run? It’s just more so just doing the right things right every day and Sunday will take care of itself.”

Following two games on the road, the Cardinals will be back at home to face the Lions on Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Eagles' decision to trade Cam Jurgens raises questions about their 2026 plans
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Tuesday, Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson retired.
item.content:encoded:
On Tuesday, Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson retired. On Wednesday, the Eagles traded center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens.

The sudden disappearance of 40 percent of the Eagles' offensive line raises obvious questions about their plans for the balance of the season.

Consider the comments from G.M. Howie Roseman after the team sent Jurgens to Baltimore.

"We weren't looking to move Cam," Roseman said, via Zach Berman of The Athletic. "Obviously, the Ravens have been looking for a center. . . . Kind of told them wasn't anything we were looking to do. Over the last 24 hours, it got to the point where we felt like it could be a win-win for them. Obviously, getting a player who's been a two-time Pro Bowl center and obviously for us, being able to get the picks we're able to get, and use that money also to sign players. Had a chance to watch Drew [Kendall] here play center is doing a nice job. Have a young player there."

The Eagles sent Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Ravens for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.

"I think for us, when you talk about the two and the five, moving from the seventh to the fifth," Roseman said. "We've had success in the fifth round, plus the money, plus you [have] Drew playing, we felt like we were getting four players for one, and just felt like for us, you know, with all these guys that we got coming up, a lot on the defensive side of the ball that we want to re-sign and want to extend, felt like that that was a good situation."

The most significant aspect of Roseman's explanation is the timing of the acceleration of the talks. "Over the last 24 hours," he said.

It points to the retirement of Johnson as the moment at which the Eagles decided to further undermine the current season in the name of setting themselves up for a brighter future. It's not tanking in the classic sense; it's a conscious, clear-eyed evaluation of the prospects of the 2026 Eagles coupled with an analysis of the future focus of the roster construction.

By moving Jurgens now (obviously, they could have traded him after the season), they maximize the return from a team that was desperate for help now at the center position, they offload the ongoing salary obligation to Jurgens, and they position themselves to keep players like cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean, both of whom are eligible for new contracts after the current season.

Still, by moving Jurgens one day after Johnson retired, it feels like the Eagles are throwing in the towel on 2026. Which opens the door to more trades that could hamper the Eagles in the short term while allowing them to properly shape the roster in the long term.

And here's the reality. The Philly defense is a strength. The offense has become a liability, with fewer than 250 yards gained in two straight games and a dismal two-for-21 showing on third down in back-to-back losses.

With the Vikings discovering that a potent defense and a no-frills offense that focuses more on protecting the ball than having explosive plays can provide a formula for winning (their streak dating back to 2025 stands at nine games), other teams will be paying attention. Which means that everyone should be paying attention to what the Eagles do between now and the trade deadline with other key pieces of an offense that is struggling to stay on the field.

item.title: In joint statement, NFL and NFLPA say drinking celebrations will be permitted
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: For "gray area" celebrations, NFL will communicate with player before fining him.
item.content:encoded:
NFL players of the world, drink up!

Celebrations may include the miming of the consumption of a beverage without fear that the league will impose discipline for the player pretending to drink the official beer of the NFL.

In a joint statement issued by the league and the NFL Players Association, it was explained that celebrations including "imitating drinking a beverage" will not be considered a violation.

Here's the full text of the statement:

"Football is the greatest game in the world. NFL players are admired by millions of fans, including young people competing at every level of the sport.

"The passion emotion, and personality players bring to the field are a big part of what makes the game special and connects them with fans worldwide. Good sportsmanship is equally important:

"To clarify the line between player expression and conduct that may result in discipline, players were reminded this week that the following are prohibited and may result in a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, a fine, or both:

"Gestures that depict violence, including the use of guns or other weapons, or gang-related signs.

"Gestures that depict smoking or drug use.

"Gestures that are sexual in nature.

"Conversely, recent celebrations imitating drinking a beverage will not be considered violations or result in discipline. The league-wide guidance provides players with greater clarity on how they can celebrate while remaining within the rules.

"When conduct falls into a gray area, the league will contact the player and provide direction before imposing discipline. The player will be advised that continued use of the identified celebration may result in future fines.

"Individual and team celebrations are part of the game and help players connect with fans. Providing clear, consistent guidance allows players to express themselves while upholding the principles of sportsmanship that have long been a hallmark of NFL football."

Beyond eliminating the Church Lady-style sensitivity to a drinking-based celebration, the league has adopted a new approach to celebrations that don't clearly violate the rules. In lieu of a fine, the league will communicate with the player. If the NFL decides that the celebration will not be allowed, the player will be fined only if he thereafter continues to do it.

It's the right result, even if it makes the sudden rash of celebration fines after Week 2 seem even more abrupt, unexpected, and flat-out bizarre.

item.title: Sean Payton: Offensive focus needs to be on details, not who calls plays
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: When the Broncos changed offensive playcallers this offseason, it guaranteed a lot of attention would be paid to how the unit fared with offensive coordinator Davis Webb calling the shots instead of head coach Sean Payton.
item.content:encoded:
When the Broncos changed offensive playcallers this offseason, it guaranteed a lot of attention would be paid to how the unit fared with offensive coordinator Davis Webb calling the shots instead of head coach Sean Payton.

The early returns have not been great. The Broncos are 27th in points and yards after a 2-2 start that has featured plenty of questions about whether Payton will be taking the job back. On Wednesday, Payton was asked at his press conference whether four games are a long enough time to evaluate Webb's performance and his answer pivoted to other matters having greater importance than who sends in a play.

"I think our focus needs to be more on the specific and the detail of each play regardless," Payton said. "I think Davis is very fast and quick and understands what we're doing. I appreciate the question, but I think that the most important job I have is really evaluating the whys. I think collectively, we all, after a game, and after a four-game sample size, certainly this isn't championship football, what we see. How quickly can we correct those things?"

Payton returned to the importance of details several times when discussing the team's offensive performance and said at one point that the team has to "become experts in the detail" in order to perform at the "championship football" level they want to reach this season. That does not preclude a change on the operations side, but Payton didn't show any cards if one is imminent in Denver.

item.title: Report: Cowboys to activate Tyler Smith for Thursday night's game
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cowboys designated Tyler Smith for return from injured reserve earlier this week and it looks like he'll be coming off that list on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys designated Tyler Smith for return from injured reserve earlier this week and it looks like he'll be coming off that list on Thursday.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that the Cowboys will activate Smith ahead of their Thursday night home game against the Buccaneers. Smith had thumb surgery ahead of the start of the regular season and was listed as questionable on the team's final injury report of the week.

Smith will likely slot back into the left guard job in his return to action. T.J. Bass has been manning the position in his place so far this season.

Wide receiver Jonathan Mingo (illness) is the only other player listed as questionable for the Cowboys for Thursday night.

item.title: Lane Johnson's retirement could create a cap mess for the Eagles in 2027
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson said in August that 2026 will probably be his last year.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson said in August that 2026 will probably be his last year. After three games, he decided to retire now.

He has an absolute right to do it. No player should continue to play pro football if he no longer wants to do it — whatever the reason(s).

The move nevertheless has financial consequences, for the Eagles and for Johnson. If he had retired after the season, and if the Eagles had waited until after June 1 to process it, the cap charges would have applied in 2027 and 2028. Now, all of the dead money will hit in 2027.

The Eagles also will have the prerogative to seek reimbursement of previously-received payments by Johnson. It gets complicated; they can recover unallocated signing bonus money and a portion of his 2026 option bonus of $21.7 million (only half of it has been paid). And recovery of the amounts they're entitled to pursue would be credited against the dead-money charges.

First, the Eagles have to decide whether they want to try to take money back from a first-ballot Hall of Famer who has meant so much to the team. While the Lions did it with both Hall of Fame running back Barry Sanders and Hall of Fame receiver Calvin Johnson, the Eagles may choose not to alienate such an important player by asking him to give money back.

Second, there's a way to finesse the situation to delay the bulk of the cap charge until 2028, in theory. If, for example, they put him on the non-football injury/illness list for the rest of the season and he officially retires after June 1, 2027, the Eagles will avoid taking the full cap charge in 2027.

The fact that the Eagles have yet to make a roster move with Johnson suggests that they're coming up with a good strategy. The best could be to delay his retirement, agree not to seek repayment of money he has earned (while possibly not paying the $10.85 million due on December 1), and finessing the cap consequences to avoid a potential mess in 2027.

item.title: Joe Burrow backtracks from "throw it more": I might have been a little emotional after the game
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: After the Bengals had just 13 designed runs for 18 yards in Sunday’s loss to the Jaguars, Joe Burrow’s response was, “Let’s throw it more.”
item.content:encoded:
After the Bengals had just 13 designed runs for 18 yards in Sunday’s loss to the Jaguars, Joe Burrow’s response was, “Let’s throw it more.”

After letting the result digest for a few days, Burrow backtracked on that sentiment in his Wednesday press conference.

“I might have been a little emotional after the game," Burrow said, via Geoff Hobson of the team’s website. Hobson noted Burrow had a wide smile when he delivered the remark. "Obviously, you want to have balance as an offense, and the run game wasn't good enough on Sunday, and I feel confident in myself that you put it in my hands and I'm going to make it work.”

The Bengals finished with just 23 total rushing yards on 15 attempts in the loss to the Jags — the lowest output of Burrow’s 81 career starts. Burrow’s 54 passing attempts were the third most he’s had in his career.

“When you get into a game like Sunday, and they're a really good defense, really good front seven, and I felt like we were moving the ball pretty well in the pass game,” Burrow said. “I could have been better in spots to help our guys and not put our defense in bad positions with the turnovers. We've got to be more balanced going forward, and a big part of that is the run game.”

To that end, Burrow noted Cincinnati may start more plays from under center instead of shotgun.

"I'm comfortable doing whatever is needed and will execute my best," Burrow said. "We obviously have to be better at it. We're still going to stick with it and keep getting reps invested in that. I think it's very valuable, so we have to be able to do it. But we need to be better.

"Under center play actions are built off the run game. Teams have to respect the run first and foremost so you don't just get jet rushers off the edge. That just puts your offensive linemen in a bad spot when they're trying to sell run but the defense isn't respecting the run and just rushing the passer. That's not a recipe for success, so that starts with the run."

The Bengals will try to get their ground game going on the road against the Dolphins in Week 5.

item.title: Odell Beckham Jr.'s arrival could be a message to Jauan Jennings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Vikings didn't sign receiver Odell Beckham Jr. for P.R. purposes.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings didn't sign receiver Odell Beckham Jr. for P.R. purposes. They signed him to help the team win games.

And they may have signed him to send a clear message to receiver Jauan Jennings.

Jennings, who signed a one-year, $8 million deal in the offseason, has yet to provide the Vikings with much of a return on their investment. In three games, he has been targeted four times, making two catches for nine yards.

On Sunday, with Justin Jefferson out, Jennings participated in 95 percent of the offensive snaps. He was targeted once.

Beckham eventually could become the No. 3 receiver, behind Jefferson and Jordan Addison. With both of them stressing defenses (and with tight end T.J. Hockenson developing into a reliable weapon for quarterback Kyler Murray), Beckham could find favorable matchups and plenty of opportunities to make plays.

If nothing else, Beckham's presence will provide a wakeup call for Jennings. Or for second-year receiver Tai Felton, who has only one catch for 14 yards on three targets in four 2026 games.

Regardless, Beckham is there for a reason. And the reason seems to be that, beyond Jefferson and Addison, the receiving corps hasn't been good enough.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers won't comment on whether play calls are coming in fast enough
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After Thursday night's loss in Cleveland, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers wasn't asked about his viral moment with coach Mike McCarthy, sparked by Rodgers's obvious frustration with the time it was taking to communicate the play call to the huddle.
item.content:encoded:
After Thursday night's loss in Cleveland, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers wasn't asked about his viral moment with coach Mike McCarthy, sparked by Rodgers’s obvious frustration with the time it was taking to communicate the play call to the huddle.

On Wednesday, Rodgers was asked several questions about the topic. Here’s the video, as posted by DK Pittsburgh Sports.

As to whether the plays are coming in "a little later than you would like," Rodgers said, "I'm not gonna touch that one."

Regarding the interaction with McCarthy, Rodgers said, "Yeah, Mike and I have talked."

It is ironed out?

"It's always ironed out," Rodgers said.

Is this the normal way they communicate?

"Sometimes, yeah," Rodgers said.

Has Rodgers found it to be effective?

"Yeah, yeah. We've had a lot of success together," Rodgers replied.

It's an issue that goes beyond the relationship between Rodgers and McCarthy. If Rodgers is behaving in a way that creates the impression that he believes McCarthy is incompetent when it comes to the simple act of quickly and efficiently telling the quarterback the next play, other players will see it. And they may view McCarthy differently.

Indeed, the fact that Rodgers wouldn't comment on whether the plays are coming in fast enough means that, in his view, they're not.

That's why McCarthy, quite frankly, shouldn't have wanted another year with Rodgers. Most of the rest of the locker room will be back next year. Rodgers won't.

The impressions of McCarthy that are influenced by the words and actions of Rodgers will linger for as long as McCarthy is the head coach.

item.title: Jesse Minter: Our offense doesn't have to change much with Tyler Huntley
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Quarterback Lamar Jackson's availability for Sunday's game against the Falcons is firmly in question as he deals with an ankle sprain.
item.content:encoded:
Quarterback Lamar Jackson's availability for Sunday's game against the Falcons is firmly in question as he deals with an ankle sprain.

But the Ravens have an experienced backup in Tyler Huntley, who is set to start if Jackson isn't ready for Week 5.

Huntley has bounced around a bit, but most of his starts have come for the Ravens since he entered the league as an undrafted free agent in 2020. While Jackson is one-of-one, Huntley’s ability and skillset translates to offensive continuity.

“I think the system of our offense and what we do does not have to change a whole lot,” head coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday when asked how much the offense varies with Huntley instead of Jackson at QB. “A lot of the plays, especially whether it’s when we are under center and running a lot of those types of things, [Huntley] can do all that. He can make a lot of those same plays.

“Obviously, Lamar’s magic is what it is. He is the best quarterback in the league for a reason. But we have a lot of confidence in ‘Snoop’ [Huntley], if that is the way it goes, to be able to really run our offense, to get the ball to our playmakers, move those guys around, find ways to get them the ball, find ways to create angles and space in the run game, and I think our offense has proven that we will be able to do that. [I’m] excited about that if that is the way it goes for him to go out there and play really well.”

After Jackson was injured, Huntley completed 8-of-9 passes for 63 yards and rushed four times for 16 yards in Sunday’s win over the Titans.

In five appearances with two starts for Baltimore last year, Huntley completed 77.6 percent of his throws for 426 yards with two touchdowns and no picks.

Baltimore is 5-6 all-time with Huntley as a starter.

item.title: Sean Payton will resume calling offensive plays for Broncos
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With the Seahawks looming, Payton will get his play-calling sea legs against the Chargers.
item.content:encoded:
The Davis Webb experiment is over.

Webb, who was promoted to offensive coordinator in the offseason and given the keys to the play-calling car, will have those keys rescinded this weekend, when the Broncos face the Chargers.

Former NFL receiver Brandon Stokley, who is now part of the morning show on 104.3 The Fan in Denver, was the first to let the cat out of the bag. "I’m hearing that Sean Payton is going to be taking over play calling this week," Stokley tweeted on Wednesday night.

We've since confirmed that, indeed, Payton will be calling the plays again.

It's been several weeks in the making, dating back to the disastrous Week 1 offensive performance against the Chiefs. In the 31-10 loss, Denver as a team had fewer yards from scrimmage (176) than Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had in his debut with the team (191).

A second-half surge against the Jaguars in Week 2 settled the situation down, temporarily. By the second half of the Week 3 game against the Rams, which Denver trailed 16-0, many were watching for indications that Payton had reclaimed the play-calling role for the second half. Again, the Broncos turned it around without Payton making the change.

In Week 4, a 3-3 halftime tie turned into a double-digit win by the 49ers. And that apparently sparked the decision to shake things up.

The timing makes sense. The Broncos face the potentially overmatched Chargers this weekend, before the Week 6 Thursday night showdown against the Seahawks. Making the move now gives Payton an opportunity to get his play-calling sea legs back before a very significant prime-time game that carries the subplot of that bizarre story from two weeks ago, when Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald's not-really-on-the-record remarks to Graham Bensinger peeled back the curtain on a dustup that emerged after the Seahawks and Broncos played in Week 1 of the 2024 season.

If the Broncos hope to once again compete for the No. 1 seed in the AFC, the margin for error has already narrowed. Last year, the Broncos finished 14-3. Through four games, they're already one defeat away from matching last year's total number of losses.

That said, the 2025 Broncos started 1-2. They responded by winning 11 in a row. Based on what we've seen through four games in 2026, however, another winning streak is unlikely — absent the change that Payton has made.

Ultimately, it's Payton's team. He needs to do whatever he thinks he should do to help the Broncos meet the high bar for 2026 that was created by their success in 2025. And the clock is ticking. Loudly.

item.title: Cam Heyward: Emotional exchanges during games nothing to "shy away" from
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: A profanity-laced exchange between Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy caught most of the attention, but it wasn't the only time things got animated for the team during last Thursday's loss to the Browns.
item.content:encoded:
A profanity-laced exchange between Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy caught most of the attention, but it wasn't the only time things got animated for the team during last Thursday's loss to the Browns.

Linebacker T.J. Watt was filmed having a lively conversation with defensive coordinator Patrick Graham over a headset at one point and defensive lineman Cam Heyward was seen doing the same with teammates on the sideline after a Browns touchdown. Heyward said on Wednesday that "there was a lot bothering me in that game" and that team leaders "shouldn’t apologize" for wearing their hearts on their sleeves during games.

“We’ve always had emotion,” Heyward said, via Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. “I don’t think that’s anything to shy away from. I’ve always been someone who tends to get a little feisty on the sideline. I’m not going to apologize for that. That’s part of the game. We hold ourselves to a high standard. We expect a lot out of our group. When we don’t, we’re pissed off because of it.”

If the "hard conversations" Heyward was talking about result in wins, the outbursts will likely be viewed as part of the process of getting the team on the same page. If not, they'll be a sign of dysfunction that threw the club off track in McCarthy's first season on the sideline.

item.title: Eagles trade Cam Jurgens to Ravens
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Baltimore has acquired the two-time Pro Bowler to help solve its injury issues along the offensive line.
item.content:encoded:
Earlier this week, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters that he was pleased with the play of offensive lineman Cam Jurgens.

But now, Jurgens is headed elsewhere.

Jurgens has been traded to the Ravens, the team announced on Wednesday.

Baltimore will receive Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.

"We are excited to acquire a two-time Pro Bowl center, Cam Jurgens, from the Eagles in a trade,” Ravens General Manager Eric DeCosta said in a statement. "Cam is a player we have long admired going all the way back to the draft process. He's a young foundational piece along our offensive line - a great scheme and cultural fit who will contribute quickly in Baltimore. We are confident that Cam will significantly impact our team and community."

Baltimore has had several injury issues on the interior of the offensive line, which Jurgens should be able to help solve.

But Jurgens is currently in concussion protocol.

The Ravens will play the Falcons on Sunday night this week.

item.title: Howie Roseman: Cam Jurgens trade can help us compete for a long period of time
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Eagles traded Jurgens to the Ravens on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles said farewell to a second starter on their offensive line in as many days when they traded Cam Jurgens to the Ravens on Wednesday.

Jurgens's departure comes a day after right tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement and General Manager Howie Roseman said on Wednesday that the deal was not a matter of the Eagles selling on this season. Roseman did say that he believes the draft picks they received in return and freeing up money for other spots was the best situation for the team moving forward.

"You can't discount opportunities that you think give you a chance to compete at a high level for a long period of time," Roseman said, via Zach Berman of TheAthletic.com.

The Eagles received a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder while sending a 2027 seventh-rounder to Baltimore along with Jurgens.

Jurgens signed a four-year contract extension with the Eagles ahead of the 2025 season and has $16 million in guaranteed money coming his way in 2027. He was the starting center when he signed that deal, but moved to left guard when Landon Dickerson was placed on injured reserve and Roseman said the Eagles think Drew Kendall "is doing a nice job" at center.

Roseman also said the team has "a lot on the defensive side of the ball that we want to re-sign and want to extend" while discussing the benefits of a deal that will be part of major changes to the makeup of the Eagles offense.

item.title: DeMeco Ryans taking back defensive play-calling for Texans
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans is taking back defensive play-calling duties, he told reporters in his Wednesday press conference.
item.content:encoded:
Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans is taking back defensive play-calling duties, he told reporters in his Wednesday press conference.

With Houston starting the season 0-4, Ryans will once again handle play-calling after relinquishing it last year to defensive coordinator Matt Burke.

But while the club finished No. 1 in scoring defense and No. 2 in yards allowed last year, the Texans are No. 20 in yards allowed and No. 26 in points allowed through the first four weeks.

Communication issues have been cited, which is part of what Ryans wants to solve by taking back the play-calling duties. He had held them for the first two-plus years of his head coaching tenure until Burke took over in September of last season.

“It all starts with me. If there’s a lack in communication, I look at myself first,” Ryans said in his press conference. “It starts with me and making sure I’m a better communicator. So just to help spark things more, I’m going to take over the play-calling for the defense and I’m going to make sure that communication is right. If our guys are saying communication is not right, then, ultimately, it falls on me. So, it’s on me to get it fixed.

“No slight against coach Burke, he’s done an outstanding job. Just want to make sure I can streamline communication in the best way possible so that isn’t the theme when I stand up here the next time I see you guys and talking about communication.”

How will things be different with Ryans calling it instead of Burke?

“We’ll see. I’m just looking for something to change,” Ryans said. “Right now, we haven’t done great the first four games, defensively, when it’s been on guys to close the game out. And it’s, man, can we spark a little change? Matt has done a good job. We’re not overhauling the defense, just trying to spark some change.”

Ryans called it a “tough decision,” but acknowledged it was one he wanted to make for the best interest of the team.

“I’m not in this role to please a lot of people’s opinion, I have to do what’s best for this team and make sure I’m leading in that way,” Ryans said. “Unfortunately, everybody isn’t happy when you make changes. When you make decisions from my chair, everybody isn’t happy. And that’s OK, because I know everything I try to do and strive to do is for the men in that locker room, to give those guys as best a chance possible to go out and win our first football game.”

While defensive play-calling has been a major part of Ryans’ coaching career, he noted he’s not necessarily excited just to be doing it again.

“It’s not about me at all. It’s about our team and how can I best help the players,” Ryans said. “That’s the reason why I’m doing this. It has nothing to do with me.”

We’ll see if Ryans taking over has an effect when the Texans face the Titans on the road in Week 5.

item.title: Malik Nabers spoke to John Harbaugh about "trying to give me the ball down the field"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers had his most productive day of the season in last Sunday's win over the Cardinals, but he said on Wednesday that he feels "like that was a basic game" rather than a breakthrough as he continues working his way back from last season's torn ACL.
item.content:encoded:
Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers had his most productive day of the season in last Sunday's win over the Cardinals, but he said on Wednesday that he feels "like that was a basic game" rather than a breakthrough as he continues working his way back from last season's torn ACL.

Nabers caught six passes for 112 yards and a touchdown that he followed up by letting head coach John Harbaugh know that he wanted the team to keep feeding him the ball. That didn't happen in the second half as Nabers only had one catch in the final 30 minutes and he explained why he was animated in discussions with the sideline in those moments.

"I felt like I didn't get targeted much after halftime," Nabers said, via a transcript from the team. "So, that was just a thing. It's just – I felt like creating explosives down the field was just helping us get in a better position to score touchdowns. Some of those plays didn't come my way, so just trying to figure out why."

Nabers revisited the issue with Harbaugh after the game and shared that the conversation was about the kinds of adjustments that the team is making during halftime.

"Just also trying to give me the ball down the field to create some of those opportunities for us to gain more points," Nabers said. "It felt like during the first half when we did that, it kind of led into the right direction with scoring touchdowns in the red zone. And just — after that, we just couldn't get going. So, I felt like the offense was needing a spark and I wanted to be that spark, so I was just trying to figure out what was going on, and what was the thought process on going into after halftime and coming out, what was the talk that he had with the coaches on implementing things down the field — we had a talk about it."

Nabers didn’t practice on Wednesday and is listed with a knee he said was "a little bit more sore" than usual. He said that they'll see how things go the rest of the week when asked if it could impact his availability against the Commanders this Sunday and that will have to play out before we find out if the Giants will be feeding their top wideout the ball more often.

item.title: Titans fire three executives, including the V.P. who oversaw the uniform change
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Titans changed their logos and uniforms this year, and now they're making changes in their front office — including firing the executive who oversaw the uniform changes.
item.content:encoded:
The Titans changed their logos and uniforms this year, and now they're making changes in their front office — including firing the executive who oversaw the uniform changes.

Erin Swartz, whose title was senior vice president of brand marketing, is out just months after the team enthusiastically unveiled the new uniforms she was in charge of redesigning. Also out are senior vice president and chief revenue officer Adam Nuse and vice president of creative Charles Jensen.

“As the Titans prepare for the opening of our new stadium and the future of Titans football, we are making changes to how we lead the business side of the organization,” the Titans said in a statement to the Nashville Tennessean. “We will hire an Executive Vice President and Chief Business Officer to lead our revenue, marketing, and communications teams. As part of these changes, Adam Nuse, Erin Swartz, and Charles Jensen are leaving the organization. We are grateful for everything they have contributed to the Titans and wish them the best in future endeavors.”

It's unclear why the three were fired. The Titans have gone through an ugly stretch on the field, finishing 3-14 each of the last two seasons and starting 0-4 this year. But the future appears bright for the business of the franchise, which is moving into a new stadium next year and will host Super Bowl LXIV in 2030.

Three team Vice Presidents, however, will not be part of that bright future.

item.title: Through four weeks of the season, zero kickoff return touchdowns
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The NFL may like to call kickoffs "Dynamic," but the most dynamic thing that can happen on a kickoff hasn't happened at all this season.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL may like to call kickoffs "Dynamic," but the most dynamic thing that can happen on a kickoff hasn't happened at all this season.

There has still not been a single kickoff return touchdown, four weeks into the 2026 NFL season. The longest kickoff return of the season was a 79-yarder by Miami's Jaylen Wright, who was knocked out of bounds at the 18-yard line at Las Vegas in Week 1.

That continues a downward trend in kickoff return touchdowns that began before the 2024 adoption of the "dynamic kickoff" and hasn't changed under the new rules, which have encouraged more returns but haven't resulted in more big plays. There were only six kickoff return touchdowns all of last season, and seven in 2024. In 2023, the last season of the old kickoff rules, there were only four touchdown returns.

Kickoff return touchdowns were once commonplace. From 2000 to 2010 there were at least a dozen kickoff return touchdowns league-wide every year. In 2007 there were 25 kickoff return touchdowns, the high-water mark for the 21st Century.

Then, in 2011, the kickoff was moved up from the 30-yard line to the 35, and kickoff return touchdowns went into a decline as more kickoffs went for touchbacks. That decline hasn't reversed with the dynamic kickoff.

For all the talk that the dynamic kickoff would make the play more exciting, it really hasn't happened. Kickoff return touchdowns are among the most exciting plays in football, but we hardly ever see them anymore.

item.title: 49ers DE Mykel Williams: "Losing my mind" with excitement for return to lineup
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: 49ers defensive end Mykel Williams's long path back to the field after last season's torn ACL is close to the finish line.
item.content:encoded:
49ers defensive end Mykel Williams's long path back to the field after last season's torn ACL is close to the finish line.

Williams is expected to be activated for this Sunday's game against the Seahawks and that would mark his first time in the team's lineup since Week 9 of last season. The 2025 first-round pick said it's been "killing me" to watch the 49ers struggle to produce a consistent pass rush with Nick Bosa out of action early this season and that he's itching to finally cut loose.

“I’m going crazy. I’m losing my mind,” Williams said, via Josh Dubow of the Associated Press. “I’m ready to go. I’m excited to play ball. I miss playing ball. It’s been like damn near a year since I played, so I just want to get back on the field.”

Williams had 20 tackles, a sack and a forced fumble before the injury ended his rookie season. In addition to rehab work, he's spent his time away from the field becoming leaner and honing in on other ways to increase his burst. Williams said "we’re going to see Sunday" if that had the desired effect and the 49ers' chances of moving to 5-0 will look a lot better if Williams hits the ground running.

item.title: Cowboys will "move pieces around" in field goal protection after blocks two weeks in a row
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer says changes are being made after the Cowboys have had field goals blocked in their last two games.
item.content:encoded:
In Week 3 against the Ravens, the Cowboys had a field goal blocked. In Week 4 against the Texans, the Cowboys had another field goal blocked — and Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said his team exploited the same flaw in the Cowboys’ protection the Ravens did. Obviously, the Cowboys have to change something.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer says they will.

Schottenheimer said that with offensive lineman Drew Shelton injured and ruled out for tonight's game against the Buccaneers, the Cowboys have to make some changes because Shelton has been part of the field goal protection unit. But Schottenheimer acknowledged that changes had to come regardless of injuries after two straight games with blocked field goals.

"Moving some pieces around, we were going to move some pieces around anyway because it hasn't been very good," Schottenheimer said. "We've got a good rotation going but at the end of the day we've just got to clean some things up from a technical standpoint."

The Cowboys are the only team in the NFL this season that has had multiple field goals blocked. That's something Schottenheimer and his staff need to get fixed, and something the Buccaneers will be well aware of heading into tonight's game.

item.title: Mike Macdonald on Joe Mixon: "Didn't work out"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Seahawks, who are thin at running back, brought Joe Mixon to town for a workout on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks, who are thin at running back, brought Joe Mixon to town for a workout on Monday. It seemed to be working out, until it wasn't.

The team ultimately didn't proceed with signing him to the practice squad, based ostensibly on his physical.

Coach Mike Macdonald was asked about the decision not to sign Mixon during Macdonald's Wednesday press conference.

“Didn’t work out," Macdonald said. "Probably the most we should say about it with respect to the process. Those things happen and it’s a part of the process.”

Mixon's health continues to be shrouded in mystery. He was on the Texans' non-football injury list for all of the 2025 season. There was never a clear answer as to what the problem was.

And so Mixon continues to be a free agent, available to sign with any team. And there are teams (like the Eagles) that need help at the position.

item.description: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans played through an injury to his ribs, catching five passes for 76 yards.
item.content:encoded:
49ers wide receiver Mike Evans played through an injury to his ribs, catching five passes for 76 yards. He did not practice two times last week before limited work on Friday.

On Wednesday, he had another limited practice.

Defensive end Nick Bosa (knee/calf), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (rest), fullback Kyle Juszczyk (knee), running back Christian McCaffrey (rest), safety Marques Sigle (ankle), cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder), defensive tackle James Thompson (ankle) and offensive tackle Trent Williams (rest) did not practice.

Running back Kaelon Black (illness) and defensive end Mykel Williams (knee) were limited.

Williams continues to work his way back from an ACL injury and expects the 49ers to activate him from the physically unable to perform list ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

item.title: Jesse Minter on Lamar Jackson: A lot of time between now and Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson didn't practice on Wednesday because of the ankle injury that has left doubt about whether he'll play against the Falcons this Sunday, but head coach Jesse Minter isn't ruling him out at this point.
item.content:encoded:
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson didn't practice on Wednesday because of the ankle injury that has left doubt about whether he'll play against the Falcons this Sunday, but head coach Jesse Minter isn't ruling him out at this point.

Minter said he wasn't worried about Jackson being prepared to play because of missed practice time and that the team isn't going to rush making any decision until they see how he responds to treatment in the coming days.

"It’s Wednesday. There’s a lot of time between now and Sunday," Minter said. "To Lamar’s credit, he’s getting a lot of treatment and doing things. There’ll be a point later in the week where we’ll kinda figure out where it’s at. . . . When he’s ready to play, he’ll be ready to play.”

Tyler Huntley will get the start for Baltimore if Jackson does not play. He was 8-of-9 for 63 yards in the second half of last Sunday's win over the Titans.

item.title: Sean Payton: I "don't think" Patrick Surtain II, Pat Bryant will land on IR
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain II and cornerback Pat Bryant suffered ankle injuries during Sunday's loss to the 49ers.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain II and cornerback Pat Bryant suffered ankle injuries during Sunday's loss to the 49ers. There has been some speculation that either or both could land on injured reserve.

Coach Sean Payton was asked about it on Wednesday.

“That’s jumping way ahead," Payton told reporters. "I don’t think so, and if they were I wouldn’t say so, but I don’t think so.”

The key words were this: "If they were I wouldn't say so." So he's not saying so. And they can delay the move until Saturday in order to start the four-game clock for their return with the Week 5 game against the Chargers.

For now, it's unlikely either will play on Sunday. (Neither practiced on Wednesday.) It's even less likely that the Broncos will disclose anything more than what the injury report requires.
